newsitem.title: UK: P&G launches detergent ads with UK shops' backing.
newsitem.headline: P&G launches detergent ads with UK shops' backing.

text.p: Procter & Gamble Co, the world's biggest advertiser, is launching a new television advertising assault in Britain for its flagship washing powder, Ariel, the U.S. group said on Monday.
The campaign, aimed at pushing forward its detergent brand in a highly competitive marketplace, takes the unusual step of carrying the endorsement of many high-street fashion retailers.

Procter & Gamble has agreed endorsements from Sears stores -- which owns the chains Warehouse, Miss Selfridge, Wallis and Selfridges. Other shops involved are women's fashion chain Laura Ashley, Principles for Men and Mothercare, it said.

The advertising, created by Saatchi & Saatchi, will initially feature all the fashion retailers in an 80 second commercial during a prime ITV viewing slot this Wednesday where they will recommend Ariel for keeping garments looking new.
No figure for the amount spent on the ads was disclosed.

"Consumers have told us that the technological benefits (of a detergent) are important, but they also want the leading names in fashion to advise them on how to care for their wardrobes," Paul Polman, vice president of Procter & Gamble UK, said.
Procter & Gamble first announced it was planning an endorsement-led campaign in May this year.
Industry observers said at the time it was responding to an estimated 25 million pounds marketing drive by its arch-rival Unilever for its relaunched Persil detergent.
